response:
I get why that phrasing sounds fairer, but I don't actually think it's more accurate — so I don't want to just swap it in.

Some people genuinely do thrive in an office, and collaboration can be easier face-to-face for certain teams. I’ll grant that. But for most knowledge work that’s mostly solo, focused tasks on a laptop, the commute and constant interruptions are a real cost, and a lot of return-to-office pushes have happened even when productivity stayed up remotely. That’s why I read them as more about visibility and control than output.

Happy to argue the specifics if you disagree, but I’d rather keep my actual take than make it sound like I think it’s a 50/50 toss-up when I don’t.
